title: Chapter 6: Bengal Renaissance & Social Reform Movement

blocks.content: The Bengal Renaissance (19th century) was one of the most important socio-cultural reform  movements in Indian history. It transformed Bengal and India with modern ideas.

cells: 1772–1833; Father of Bengal Renaissance; founded Brahmo Sabha (1828); abolished Sati; pioneer of modern India
Founded 1828 by Ram Mohan Roy; reformed Hindu society; against idol worship & caste
1809–31; Derozian movement; free thinking; Young Bengal movement
1820–91; reformed education; widow remarriage; simplified Bengali script; championed women's education
1863–1902; born Narendranath Datta, Kolkata; founded Ramakrishna Mission (1897); Chicago Speech 1893
1836–86; spiritual master; Dakshineswar temple; Vivekananda's guru
1824–73; first Bengali to adopt Western literary forms; "Meghnad Vadh Kavya"
1838–94; wrote "Anandamath"; composed "Vande Mataram"; father of Bengali novel
1861–1941; Nobel Prize 1913; wrote national anthems of India & Bangladesh; Shantiniketan
1897–1945; INA; Azad Hind Fauj; "Give me blood, I will give you freedom"

[EXAM TIP] Rabindranath Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana (India's national anthem) AND Amar Sonar Bangla (Bangladesh's national anthem). He was the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize (1913). Asked very frequently.
